newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-CAPOBIANCO LOSES FIGHT OVER FOUR-YEAR BAN.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-CAPOBIANCO LOSES FIGHT OVER FOUR-YEAR BAN.

text.p: Australian sprinter Dean Capobianco has lost his fight against a four-year ban for a positive drug test.
International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) president Primo Nebiolo said on Saturday a petition by Capobianco for reinstatement in competition had been rejected.
"We did not accept his request. The (ban) decision is irrevocable," Nebiolo told a news conference after an IAAF meeting.
Capobianco was banned for four years after he tested positive for the steroid Stanozol at a meeting on May 27, 1996, in Hengelo, the Netherlands.
But one day before that meeting he raced in Dijon, France, and was tested to be drug free.
Capobianco asked for the Dijon sample to be preserved but his request was overlooked and the test destroyed.
He has accused the IAAF of destruction of evidence and his request for reinstatement was backed by the Australian Olympic Committee.
